Every observable hop rests on verified findings: F11/F23 show host-level connect timeouts and 503s against api.exchange-partner.example affecting BOTH exchange-gateway operations (placeOrder + quoteSnapshot, i.e. traffic with no order-service relationship); F21 shows that deepest error (11:01:25Z) precedes order-service's first 504 (11:02:45Z); F10/F20 show exchange-gateway error ~40% and p99 ~5s onset in the 11:00Z bucket; F8/F22 show 100% of order-service's 349 errors are outbound exchange-gateway 504s with no app-side/DB/idempotency signature; F14 shows failures persisted ~1h40m past the 11:16Z rollback. H2/H3/H5 are each contradicted by specific evidence (F8/F22/F13/F14; F7/F15 ordering; F12/F8). H4's distinguishing mechanism — a shared component degrading multiple consumers at the same onion — is refuted by F19/F20 (market-data-service, the other exchange-gateway caller, stays flat ~39ms p99 with a tiny 2-min-later bump) and F23 (host-level partner failure independent of the order path). The single unmeasured hop (the partner's own degradation) is structurally unobservable (has_telemetry=false, no status-page tool, F28/F17) and is corroborated by two independent in-band signals; this ceiling justifies a confidence cap, not further querying. The shared-datastore sweep remains incomplete but a selective exchange-path-only datastore fault is not constructible and would not change the ranking, so it is a low-severity residual rather than a blocker.
